### Round log

- G1R2: E0002, a minimal version of E0001, built OK. Estimates moved but the physical plan did NOT change, so there was no gain. RETIRED. The premise was wrong.

- Keep diffs out of widely included headers (long rebuilds). Use file-local statics or constexpr.
- Ask implementers to build in the background and to EXPLAIN-check before the full bench.
- CHEAP EXPERIMENTS: `dbe-tool sql "SET <setting>=X; <query>; <query>"` prints per-statement ms (first run cold, second hot). Use it to time subqueries in isolation; it is very effective.
- rules.md item 4: never change default settings.
- Planner estimates after LIKE filters and outer joins are off by 5-1000x. Prefer runtime-adaptive mechanisms.
- The bar is -2.7% visible geomean. A 20% gain on one of 14 templates (about -1.6%) does NOT clear it. Cut a big template by 30%+ or help several.
- VERIFY probe/build sides in the plan BEFORE proposing join ideas. Two retirements came from misreading sides.

### Tooling facts
- EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON) hangs. EXPLAIN ANALYZE via `dbe-tool sql` works.
- profile.md truncates big plans. Operator times are summed CPU.
- Bench noise is about ±10% per query on quick runs.

### Codebase facts (verified)
- HASH_JOIN: the LEFT child is the probe and the RIGHT child is the build. BFs only reach probe-side scans.
- Join BF: CanUseBloomFilter physical_hash_join.cpp:761 requires conditions.size()==1. E0005 has a working per-key BF design (see ledger) if a use appears.
- LIKE: LikeMatcher is already good. FSST scan decompresses every row.
- RelationStatisticsHelper::DEFAULT_SELECTIVITY=0.2 applies flat to non-equality filters.
- Perfect hash agg: CanUsePerfectHashAggregate plan_aggregate.cpp:127, threshold :230. E0004 had a working lazy version.
  - q13 inner agg forced perfect 115→90ms. A 20-bit table on empty input costs +10ms.
- Radix HT adaptation: DecideAdaptation radix_partitioned_hashtable.cpp:424.
- Agg HT: GroupedAggregateHashTable::AddChunk aggregate_hashtable.cpp:519 → TryAddCompressedGroups (constant/dictionary fast paths) → FindOrCreateGroupsInternal :641 (probe loop with a sel_vector IsSet template variant, RowMatcher compare, skip_lookups branch :685) → UpdateAggregates :533.

### Profile hotspots (G3R2, geomean 43.5ms)
- q09 121ms, q13 105, q18 87, q16 49, q19 47, q22 43, q03 39, rest 22-37ms.
- q09: the join operator is dominated by building an 800k-row partsupp HT; lineitem scan 0.43s.
- q13: orders scan + NOT LIKE 0.22s, RIGHT join 0.10-0.15s, HASH_GROUP_BY 0.20s.

- Active: run collapse for clustered agg keys (G3R2). If the gain is real but small, combine it with E0004's lazy perfect HT (the q13 win) into one aggregation bundle. - Exhausted: cardinality-selectivity tweaks for q09; estimate-gated perfect hashing; standalone lazy perfect HT; multi-key BF for q09.

issues.title: Collapse adjacent duplicate group keys before hash-table probe in aggregation
issues.hypothesis: q18 (87ms, 3rd slowest) is dominated by the subquery `SELECT l_orderkey FROM lineitem GROUP BY l_orderkey HAVING sum(l_quantity)>312`. Measured with dbe-tool sql: that aggregate takes ~65-72ms hot. A plain sum(l_quantity) scan of lineitem takes 3ms, so nearly all of the time is in GroupedAggregateHashTable (6M rows, 1.5M groups). lineitem is stored clustered by l_orderkey (about 4 consecutive rows per key), so roughly 75% of input rows have the same group key as the row before them. Today each of those rows still pays the full FindOrCreateGroupsInternal path (aggregate_hashtable.cpp:641-814): offset/salt computation, the inner probe loop with a random cache-missing access into `entries`, and a RowMatcher compare against the materialized group row. If equal adjacent keys are detected with a cheap sequential compare of the input vector, only the run heads need to be probed, and the other rows copy the head's address. Clustered or sorted keys are common: order ids, time-series ingestion order, and join outputs that keep probe-side order (for example GROUP BY l_orderkey after a join probed by lineitem in q03-style queries).
issues.plan: In src/execution/aggregate_hashtable.cpp, GroupedAggregateHashTable::FindOrCreateGroupsInternal, after the hashes and addresses vectors are flattened and before the probe loop (i.e. not in the skip_lookups branch), add a file-local static helper that builds a selection of run heads. Row r is a duplicate of r-1 when hashes[r]==hashes[r-1] and every group column is equal at r and r-1, checked with the UnifiedVectorFormat already produced by TupleDataCollection::ToUnifiedFormat (state.partitioned_append_state.chunk_state.vector_data): null-ness must match, and both values are equal or both NULL. Restrict this to group columns of fixed-size physical types (numerics, dates, hugeint) plus string_t compared via Equals; otherwise skip the fast path. If the number of duplicates is 0 (or below about chunk_size/8), use the existing path unchanged. Otherwise run the existing loop with `sel_vector` pointing at a heads SelectionVector and `remaining_entries = head_count` (the inner loop already has a sel_vector->IsSet() template variant, and new_groups_out/empty_vector indices are original row indices, so appends are unaffected). After the loop, fill addresses[r] = addresses[r-1] for each duplicate r in ascending order. Make it adaptive with a member or AggregateHTAppendState counter: after ~16 chunks with less than 1/8 duplicates, disable the check for that hash table, so unclustered inputs pay only a short trial cost. If a new member is needed, put it in AggregateHTAppendState or the GroupedAggregateHashTable header (src/include/duckdb/execution/aggregate_hashtable.hpp) and accept the rebuild; build in the background. UpdateAggregates already handles repeated addresses, as today's path produces them for in-chunk duplicates. Verify q18 with EXPLAIN ANALYZE and check that the results are identical. Also run a GROUP BY with NULL keys and with a multi-column key (l_orderkey, l_linenumber) for correctness.
issues.expected_gain: q18 -15 to -25% (the subquery aggregate is ~70% of its time; probe+compare work drops for ~75% of rows). Small gains are possible on q03, q04 and q18's outer aggregates and on any GROUP BY over join output that keeps lineitem/orders order. Roughly -1.5 to -3% visible geomean.
issues.generality: Any hash aggregate (and DISTINCT, which shares FindOrCreateGroups) whose input has runs of equal keys: sorted or clustered tables, data loaded in time order, joins that keep probe order, and low-cardinality keys in sorted data. Queries on randomly ordered keys pay one sequential compare per row for the first ~16 chunks, after which the check is disabled. That cost is negligible, but tiny aggregates with a high chunk count over random data could see under 1% overhead.
issues.risk: Medium-low. The logic is local to one function and correctness is easy to test (results must match exactly). The main risks are NULL handling in the adjacency compare and interaction with the unpartitioned_data path that uses empty_vector indices. Both are covered by keeping original row indices. Performance risk is small because of the adaptive disable.
